newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded, bids pulled in several months.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded, bids pulled in several months.

text.p: The IPE's natural gas contract was untraded on Tuesday morning, with only one trade now seen so far this week.

That was a deal done for December at 14 pence a therm on Monday, but the bid/offer spread for that month ballooned on Tuesday morning. It was bid at 13.85 pence a therm and offered at 15 pence by the close of the morning session, among the widest bid/offer spreads posted for any month.

Offers were posted for the first eleven months by the close, with bids only seen for seven. Front month July was unbid, but for other months where both bids and offers were posted, they straddled the previous settlement level.

The High Court ruled on Tuesday morning in favour of the CATS (Central Area Transmission System) parties in the dispute between CATS and Enron over the Capacity Reservation and Transportation Agreement between the two sides for gas from the North Sea's J-Block.

But the ruling had no impact on price levels, with dealers on the OTC market saying that the market had already factored in the expected settlement of all areas of the J-Block dispute as prices fell heavily last Friday.
